chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi al-Nahwi al-Tamimi reported to me, he said: Hisham ibn Yunus al-Nahshali narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Ya'la narrated to us, from Humaid al-A'raj, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud who said:

The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: How surprising is the heedless one, while he himself is not neglected [by God]; and how surprising is the one chasing the worldly life, while death chases him; and how surprising is the one who laughs heartily, while he does not know whether Allah is pleased with him or is displeased with him.

key_terms.الدنيا: The worldly life, the temporal world as opposed to the hereafter
key_terms.سخط: Divine displeasure, wrath — the opposite of God's pleasure (ridha)
key_terms.غافل: Heedless, negligent — one who is unmindful of God's observation and the afterlife
key_terms.مغفول: Neglected, overlooked — implying God never neglects or overlooks anyone

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about heedlessness and chasing the worldly life?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition narrated through Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) expresses astonishment at three types of human behavior that reflect spiritual negligence. The hadith was delivered as a rhetorical admonition to awaken the believers from heedlessness (ghafla), reminding them that God constantly observes them, death is inevitable, and their ultimate fate before God remains unknown. The original audience understood this as a call to constant self-examination and vigilance.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 9. He said: Abul Hasan Muhammad B. Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi al-Nahwi al-Tamimi reported to me from Hisham ibn Yunus al-Nahshali, who reported to me from Yahya ibn Ya’la, from Hameed al-A’raj, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Abdullah ibn Masood that:

The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said: "I am surprised at the heedless person who is not without survelance; I am surprised at the one chasing the world, while death chases him; I am surprised at a person having a loud, hearty laugh, while he does not know whether Allah is pleased with him or is displeased."
